newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard-right welcomes Prodi speech.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard-right welcomes Prodi speech.

text.p: Rightist leader Gianfranco Fini welcomed an offer by Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday to put his future on the line if his hard-left ally failed to back him on policy towards Albania.

Fini's National Alliance party is part of the main opposition Freedom Alliance, whose leaders were meeting after the speech to decide whether to back the government in a parliamentary vote to send an Italian-led force to Albania.

"Having always said that we needed to deploy the mission but also needed to certify the division in the (governing) majority, I personally feel more than satisfied" with the speech, Fini told reporters.

Prodi's government lacks a majority in the lower house, where the vote was due later on Wednesday, without its ally Communist Refoundation, which confirmed after the speech that it still intended to vote 'no' to the force.

Prodi appealed in his speech to all parties to back the government motion and said he would go immediately to President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro if Refoundation persisted in its dissent and ask the head of state to rule on the next step.
Scalfaro has several options available. He can ask Prodi to offer his resignation or send him back to parliament for a confidence vote.
Refoundation says it will back the government in a confidence test as long as it is not on Albania.
It sees the Albanian proposal as neo-colonialist. Fifty-eight years ago this week Fascist Italy invaded Albania.
